subject: Deployment route confirmation and migration handoff

Subject: Follow-up: hosting preferences & migration constraints (post-demo)

Neha — thanks again for the demo earlier today. A few rapid follow-ups from our side after syncing with infra and security: 

1) Hosting preference: our infra lead asked if you can confirm the migration patterns you see most often for customers coming from other LLM APIs vs. customers coming from self-hosted/legacy GPU clusters.

2) Data residency & KMS: we need to confirm that if we go Private (VPC/on-prem) we can bring our own KMS and that audit logs will be retained for 12 months.

3) Can you outline the recommended cutover approach for our use case (real-time clinical summarization) — specifically we want minimal latency regression and a fallback plan if throughput spikes.

Also attaching the procurement checklist — we looped in procurement in case there are contract-level questions. Looking for a short doc or checklist we can show our infra/engineering leads.

Best,
Elaine Park
Head of Platform Integrations
Atlas Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: hosting preferences & migration constraints (post-demo)

Hi Elaine — really appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick answers up front, then a short proposed next step list and a one-page attachment we maintain for handoffs.

High-level migration patterns we commonly see (short):
- From other LLM APIs: majority choose a staged routing approach — start with shadowing/traffic mirroring to validate outputs, then progressive traffic shift (canary) to Hosted API or Dedicated depending on SLA/cost needs. Typical timeline 2–6 weeks for production-quality alignment.
- From self-hosted or legacy GPU clusters: teams often prefer Dedicated or Private to preserve control. Common path is a hybrid: run inference in Dedicated while gradually moving stateful/ops pieces (metrics, caching) to Redwood; final cutover can involve adapter layer to translate KV formats and tokenization differences. Timeline usually 6–12 weeks.

Data residency & KMS:
- Private (VPC/on-prem): BYOK with standard KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, customer HSM). Audit logs and access trails can be retained to your retention window — we can set the default to 12 months and export to your SIEM.

Cutover recommendations for low-latency clinical summarization:
1) Start with a test routing layer that mirrors 10–20% of requests to Redwood (no user-impact). Use our mismatch reporting to tune prompts/temperature.
2) Enable prefix caching for common templates and KV cache warm-up to reduce tail latency on first requests.
3) Move to Dedicated if sustained QPS requires predictable SLOs — Dedicated reduces jitter and gives you a predictable token cost model.
4) Canary + automatic fallback: configure canary at 5–10% then 25% before 100%; set an automatic fallback policy to your origin (legacy cluster) on error rate or latency thresholds.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll attach a one-pager (redwood-deploy-options-one-pager.pdf) summarizing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for procurement/infra.
- Jonas (cc’d) can run a short cost/latency estimate if you share projected QPS and 95th pct latency targets.
- Marissa can coordinate a technical handoff call with your infra + security to validate KMS and audit export specifics.

If this looks good, can we schedule a 30‑minute handoff on Tue/Wed next week?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-deploy-options-one-pager.pdf
From: Elaine Park <elaine@atlashealth.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: hosting preferences & migration constraints (post-demo)

Thanks Neha — that’s exactly the level we needed. A couple clarifications from infra/security after reading your note: 

- For the mirror approach, is there support for token-level logging being redacted before export? We cannot have PHI leave the cluster unredacted during mirror.
- For Dedicated, what is the commitment cadence (monthly/quarterly) and is burst capacity priced separately?

QPS estimate for a single region (initial): 50 sustained qps, 120 p95 latency target, peak burst to 200 qps for short periods (5–10 minutes).

We are available Tue 2027-05-04 11:00-13:00 or Wed 2027-05-05 09:00-11:00 PT for a handoff. Which slot works for your team?

—Elaine
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: hosting preferences & migration constraints (post-demo)

Elaine — great, thanks for the QPS and the questions. Short answers and confirmed slot below.

- Token-level logging & PHI: we support configurable redaction rules for mirrored traffic. For Private deployments you can keep the mirror inside your VPC so no PHI leaves your network. For Hosted/Dedicated we can enable on-the-fly redaction before logs are persisted/exported. We'll capture the exact redaction rules during the security call.
- Dedicated commitments: flexible monthly and annual reserved options; burst capacity is available as an add-on with transparent billing — Jonas will include a sample pricing tranche for your QPS profile.

Confirmed: Tue 2027-05-04 11:30 PT for the 30-minute technical handoff. Jonas will send a calendar invite and an initial estimate doc prior to the call. Marissa will run procurement pre-reads.

Action items assigned: 
- Jonas: cost/latency estimate for 50 sustained qps + burst to 200 qps (deliver before handoff).
- Marissa: prepare procurement checklist + sample SOW language covering BYOK and audit retention.
- Neha: prepare a short migration playbook (shadow → canary → cutover) and redaction examples.

See you Tue — sending invites now.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
